evals.name: linear-github-lifecycle primary scenario
evals.prompt: Take accepted Linear issue ENG-205 all the way from start of work through to a merged PR and Linear disposition.
evals.expected_output: Composes the 7 focused Wave 2 skills (work-to-development, development-to-pr, pr-to-linear, merge-to-completion, status-and-learning, linear-github-linking for resume reads, plus linear-github-reconciliation on demand) in the documented phase order, delegating each phase's actual logic rather than reimplementing it; gets confirmation at phase transitions.

evals.name: linear-github-lifecycle "take this accepted issue all the way to merge" trigger
evals.prompt: Take this accepted issue all the way to merge — Linear issue ENG-311, 'Add rate limiting to the public API', is already Accepted. Run it through to a merged PR and Linear disposition.
evals.expected_output: Activates on this exact declared trigger phrase and delegates each lifecycle phase to its own named focused skill (work-to-development, development-to-pr, pr-to-linear, merge-to-completion, status-and-learning) in the documented phase order, rather than performing any phase's logic itself; fires an AskUserQuestion confirmation gate at each phase transition, additive to each delegated skill's own internal gate.

evals.name: linear-github-lifecycle "resume this interrupted Wave 2 lifecycle run" trigger
evals.prompt: Resume this interrupted Wave 2 lifecycle run for Linear issue ENG-288. The git-github-evidence array shows, in order: a work-started entry (repository acme/api, branch feat/eng-288-webhook-retries), a commit-linked entry for the same branch, and a pr-published entry for the same branch whose gates[] array is [{name: lint, result: pass}, {name: unit-tests, result: pass}]. No pr-ready or pr-merged entry exists. The issue currently shows status 'In Review' in Linear. Continue the lifecycle from here.
evals.expected_output: Activates on this exact declared trigger phrase, applies Resume Behavior to determine the furthest-completed phase (Commit + gates + Publish, via the pr-published entry) and correctly identifies Review/fix + Ready (pr-to-linear) as the resume point without re-running already-completed phases; presents the resume point to the user via AskUserQuestion before continuing rather than silently resuming; treats the Issue's 'In Review' Linear status as informative context only, never as proof of phase completion.

evals.name: Frontmatter-description vs. declared-trigger-phrase consistency (Quick Workflow, methodology note below)
evals.prompt: For each phrase in this skill's own '## Testing & Validation' > 'Verify this skill activates on' list, would this skill's frontmatter description plausibly trigger on it?
evals.expected_output: Every declared positive trigger phrase maps to vocabulary actually present in the frontmatter description.

methodology_note_eval_4: This run's with_skill grading was performed directly by the orchestrating fork (a 'Do NOT spawn subagents' hard rule barred the normal Agent-tool dispatch this pipeline's WITH_SKILL_ONLY template calls for) via description-vs-trigger-phrase textual/semantic consistency checking, not a full agentic task simulation. No SKILL.md content changed this session -- this run's purpose was a sanity check that adding scripts/smoke_test.py to each skill didn't coincide with any drift between the skill's own documented trigger claims and its frontmatter, not a search for new behavioral defects.
